questions.title: Main product lines
questions.story: What product lines does AdventureWorks sell? List the categories and the sub-categories.

questions.title: Where the company operates
questions.story: Where does AdventureWorks operate? Return the territory, the country and the region group.

questions.title: Why customers buy
questions.story: Why do customers buy from AdventureWorks? List the purchase reasons.

questions.title: Wrongly priced products
questions.story: A colleague named Peter set the wrong price on some products that have already been sold. A wrong price means a unit price above 3,500. List the orders that contain these products, so the product team can review them.

questions.title: Refund for customer 29641
questions.story: Customer 29641 called and wants a refund for the order shipped on 2013-06-06. Check the order value (SubTotal) so the customer service team can handle the ticket.

questions.title: Cards ending in 9916
questions.story: The card partner reports that cards ending in 9916 are fraudulent. List the orders paid with these cards, so the risk team can review them.
questions.hint: The card number is in the CardNumber column of ADW_Dim_CreditCard. Work in two steps.

steps.title: Step 1: find the cards ending in 9916
Step 2: find the orders paid with those cards

questions.title: Highest standard costs
questions.story: The Finance team is reviewing production costs. List the 10 products with the highest standard cost, and show the ratio of standard cost to list price for each.
questions.note: rows tie on StandardCost at the 10th place, so only the cost column is compared

questions.title: Promotions for resellers
questions.story: Which promotions do we run for resellers? Return the special offer ID and its description.

questions.title: Two customer groups in one query
questions.story:
The Customer Research team is studying customers in different regions. Find the customers who bought in 2012 and fit one of these two groups:
- Online buyers in Canada or France, with an order value of at least 1,000.
- Offline buyers in the US or Australia, with an order value between 600 and 1,000.
Return CustomerID, TerritoryID, ship date, order value and the online/offline flag.
questions.hint: Both groups must come back from one query.

questions.title: Online in Q4 2013 or offline in Q1 2012
questions.story: The Customer Research team wants to compare online and offline buyers. Find the customers who bought offline in Q1 2012, or online in Q4 2013. Return CustomerID, order year, order quarter and the online/offline flag.

questions.title: Won deals above list price
questions.story: List the deals won in 2017 whose closing value is higher than the list price of the product.

questions.title: Regions that lost deals in Q1 2017
questions.story: Which regions had agents who lost deals in the first three months of 2017?

questions.title: Products sold to the marketing sector
questions.story: Which products were sold to companies in the marketing sector in won deals in 2017?

questions.title: Sectors of the top 10 deals
questions.story: Which sectors do the 10 highest-value deals of all time belong to?

questions.title: Fastest and slowest deals
questions.story: Which 10 deals closed fastest and which 10 closed slowest?

questions.title: Europe customers on Vista or SuperiorCard
questions.story: The Payment team is running a survey in Europe. List the customers who bought in Europe in Q3 2013 and paid with a Vista or SuperiorCard. Return the CustomerID and the card type.
questions.hint: When a question is only about orders, ADW_Sales_orders is the base table.

questions.title: Black or Silver Mountain Bikes with cost 1,000 to 1,500
questions.story: The Product team wants a list of Mountain Bikes that are Black or Silver and have a standard cost between 1,000 and 1,500. Also show the ratio of standard cost to list price for each product.

questions.title: Orders of the top 10 customers of 2011 and 2012
questions.story: The company wants to thank its biggest spenders of 2011 and 2012. Get every order (order ID, customer ID and total due) of the top 10 customers of each year.
questions.hint: The customer lists are in the tables ADW_Top_10_spending_cust_2011 and ADW_Top_10_spending_cust_2012.

questions.title: Customers in the top 10 in both years
questions.story: How many customers are in the top 10 spenders of both 2011 and 2012?

questions.title: Orders bought for quality or supplier reputation
questions.story: The company wants to study buying behaviour. Find the orders placed for the reasons Quality or Manufacturer (supplier reputation) in 2012 and 2013.

questions.title: Sold above 2,000 with a special offer
questions.story: The Business team wants to design a promotion for high-value purchases. Find the products that have been sold at a unit price above 2,000 and carried a special offer. Return ProductID and ProductName.

questions.title: Bikes and Clothing sold under a Volume Discount
questions.story: The Bikes and Clothing categories are planned for a cross-sell campaign. Find the names of the products in these two categories that sold under a Volume Discount offer.

questions.title: Monthly revenue and profit report
questions.story: The board wants an overview of revenue, profit, profit margin and number of customers by month and year, across the four years the company has operated. Build the report.

questions.title: Performance by country
questions.story: Build the same report by country and year: revenue, profit, customers and profit margin. Which country performs best and most steadily?

questions.title: Revenue by payment method
questions.story: How much revenue does each payment method bring in, in each country?

questions.title: Online share of revenue, 2013 vs 2014
questions.story: Compare the share of revenue that comes from the online channel in each country in 2013 and 2014. Where does online do best?
questions.hint: Use conditional aggregation to calculate online revenue as a share of total revenue.

questions.title: Weekdays vs weekends in the US
questions.story: The company wants to compare sales on weekdays and weekends in the US. For each US territory, compare the average quantity sold (OrderQty) per day and per customer on weekdays versus weekends. What do you notice in the numbers?
questions.hint: Use DATEPART together with CASE WHEN to label each day as a weekday or a weekend.

questions.title: Buying behaviour, US vs EU
questions.story: The Customer Research team wants to compare buying behaviour in the US and the EU. Compare purchase frequency (orders per customer) and average quantity per order. Which region does better?

questions.title: Which category to push in Europe
questions.story: If the company wants to push one category in Europe, which one should it be?
questions.hint: This is an open question. Look at it from more than one angle, for example revenue, profit and profit margin.

questions.title: Customers with AOV above the US AOV
questions.story: The company wants to target customers whose average order value (AOV) is higher than the AOV of customers who buy in the US, to study how to raise AOV. List these customers.
questions.hint: AOV = total value of all orders divided by the number of orders.

questions.title: Bikes only, Clothing only, or both
questions.story:
Split customers into three groups and compare the average order value (AOV) of their Bikes and Clothing purchases.
- Group 1: bought only Bikes.
- Group 2: bought both Bikes and Clothing.
- Group 3: bought only Clothing.

questions.title: Year-over-year growth by country
questions.story: Calculate year-over-year revenue growth (% YoY) by country for 2012 to 2014. Which country grows fastest?

questions.title: Sub-categories with rising promotion cost
questions.story: The company is reviewing the total promotion cost of its sub-categories. List the sub-categories whose total promotion cost rose two years in a row.
questions.hint: It works like the year-over-year question (HW 3).

questions.title: Running revenue by category
questions.story: Review the accumulated (running) revenue of each category, month by month within each year. Build the report.
questions.hint: Use an aggregate window function.

questions.title: Best-selling product by country
questions.story: Which product sold the most units in each country?

questions.title: Month-over-month growth by category
questions.story: Calculate month-over-month (MoM) revenue growth for each category across the years. January must be compared with the previous December.

questions.title: Spending above the Clothing median
questions.story: Find the customers whose total spending across all categories is above the 50th percentile of spending among Clothing customers.
questions.hint:
Step 1: find the 50th percentile of spending among Clothing customers (expected output: one number) with PERCENT_RANK().
Step 2: calculate each customer's total spending in all categories and keep the customers above the number from step 1.

questions.title: Most popular payment method
questions.story: Which payment method is the most popular by number of orders in each country and year? If you rank by total revenue instead, does the order change?

questions.title: Top 5 promoted products by territory
questions.story: Review the promotion programme of each territory. For each territory, list the 5 products with the highest share of units sold with a promotion.

questions.title: Orders with no salesperson
questions.story: Finance wants to know how many orders were placed without a salesperson, to see how much revenue comes from direct sales. Return the number of orders with no salesperson and the total number of orders.
questions.hint: Run SELECT DISTINCT SalesPersonID FROM ADW_Sales_orders first and read the values. In this database a missing salesperson is stored as the text 'NULL', so IS NULL finds nothing.

questions.title: Products with no colour
questions.story: The product team wants to see how many products there are in each colour. Products with a missing colour should show as 'Unknown'. Return the colour and the number of products.
questions.hint: As in the last question, a missing colour is the text 'NULL'. Replace it with CASE WHEN, then group by the new column.

questions.title: Fix the typos in the account list
questions.story: Sales Ops found spelling mistakes in the account list. Return every account with a clean sector and a clean office location. Change 'technolgy' to 'technology' and 'Philipines' to 'Philippines', and keep every other value as it is.
questions.hint: Run SELECT DISTINCT sector FROM CRM_Accounts and SELECT DISTINCT office_location FROM CRM_Accounts first, and read each list slowly.

questions.title: Deals lost in a join
questions.story: In Lesson 3 you listed the 2017 won deals priced above the list price and got 1,674. That count missed deals, because the pipeline writes one product as 'GTXPro' and the product list writes 'GTX Pro'. Fix the name and join again. For won deals closed in 2017, return three numbers: how many deals there are, how many found a list price, and how many closed above the list price.
questions.hint: Use REPLACE(product, 'GTXPro', 'GTX Pro') in the join condition. After the fix, the number of deals that found a price should equal the number of won deals.
questions.note: 4,238 deals, 4,238 with a price, 2,040 above list price

questions.title: Customers by age group
questions.story: Marketing plans an age-based campaign. In GBE_Customers the birthday is stored as text, for example 7/3/1939. Convert it to a date and work out each customer's age on 2020-01-01. Then count customers in four groups: Under 30, 30-49, 50-69 and 70+. Return the group name and the number of customers.
questions.hint: CONVERT(date, Birthday, 101) turns text like 7/3/1939 into a date. CAST(Birthday AS DATE) does not work on this format here.

questions.title: Repeated customer names
questions.story: The data team thinks GBE_Customers contains duplicate customers, because 15,266 customers have only 15,118 different names. Check it. For each name that appears more than once, return the name, how many times it is listed, and how many different birthdays it has.
questions.hint: GROUP BY Name with HAVING COUNT(*) > 1. COUNT(DISTINCT Birthday) counts the different birthdays.
questions.note: 137 names, each repeat has a different birthday

questions.title: Orders far above average
questions.story: Finance wants to review unusually large orders before the monthly report. Flag an order as an outlier when its TotalDue is more than 2 standard deviations above the average TotalDue of all orders. Return how many orders are flagged and how many orders there are in total.
questions.hint: STDEV(TotalDue) gives the standard deviation. Calculate the average and STDEV in a CTE or subquery, then compare each order with average + 2 x STDEV.

questions.title: Two ways to find outliers
questions.story: Repeat the outlier check with the IQR rule. An order is an outlier when TotalDue is above Q3 + 1.5 x IQR, where IQR = Q3 - Q1. Compare the number of flagged orders with the standard deviation method from the last question. Which method flags more orders, and why? Would you remove these orders? Write your conclusion below.
questions.hint: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.25) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY TotalDue) OVER () gives Q1. Use 0.75 for Q3.

questions.title: Validate the cleaned accounts
questions.story: Before you share the cleaned account list from the typo question, validate it. Return one row with four numbers: the total number of rows, the number of different accounts, the rows where the sector is still 'technolgy', and the rows where the office location is still 'Philipines'.
questions.hint: Rebuild the cleaned list in a CTE, then count on top of it. The validation must run on the cleaned data, not on CRM_Accounts.

questions.title: R, F and M for every customer
questions.story: Marketing wants to segment customers by how recently, how often and how much they buy. Start with the raw numbers. For every customer in ADW_Sales_orders, return Recency (days between the customer's last order and 2014-07-01), Frequency (number of orders) and Monetary (total TotalDue).
questions.hint: DATEDIFF(day, MAX(OrderDate), '2014-07-01'), COUNT(DISTINCT SalesOrderID) and SUM(TotalDue), all grouped by CustomerID.

questions.title: Score each customer from 1 to 5
questions.story: Turn the three numbers into scores. For each customer, calculate PERCENT_RANK for Recency, Frequency and Monetary, then cut each percentile into five bands: up to 0.2 is 1, up to 0.4 is 2, up to 0.6 is 3, up to 0.8 is 4, and above 0.8 is 5. A recent customer must get a high Recency score, so rank Recency from the most days to the fewest (ORDER BY Recency DESC). Return CustomerID, R_score, F_score and M_score.
questions.hint: Put the R, F and M calculation from the last question in a CTE. Then use three PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ...) columns and a CASE WHEN for each band.

questions.title: Size and value of each segment
questions.story:
Marketing needs a simple segment list. Using the scores from the last question, put each customer in the first segment they match:
- Champions: R, F and M scores are all 4 or 5.
- Loyal: F score is 4 or 5.
- Promising: R score is 4 or 5.
- At Risk: M score is 4 or 5.
- Hibernating: everyone else.
For each segment, return the number of customers, the number of orders and the total revenue (TotalDue).
questions.hint: A CASE WHEN checks the conditions from top to bottom, and the first true one wins. Join the segments back to ADW_Sales_orders on CustomerID to count orders and add up revenue.

questions.title: How each segment buys
questions.story: The CRM team asks if there is any notable buying behaviour in each segment. For each segment from the last question, return the average order value (AOV), the number of orders per customer and the share of orders placed online. Then write two findings and one action for the team.
questions.hint: AOV = total TotalDue divided by the number of orders. The online share uses OnlineOrderFlag, which is 1 for online orders.
questions.note: Champions AOV 11,035; At Risk 2,652; Loyal 2,509; Promising 606; Hibernating 230

questions.title: Favourite category of each segment
questions.story: Which product category brings the most revenue in each segment? Return the segment, the category, the revenue (LineTotal) and the category's share of the segment's revenue, ranked within each segment. Does any segment buy differently from the others?
questions.hint: Join the segments to the orders, the order lines, the products, the sub-categories and the categories. Use SUM(LineTotal) OVER (PARTITION BY segment) for the share.

questions.title: First purchase month
questions.story: Retention analysis starts by putting each customer in a cohort, which is the month of their first order. For every customer in ADW_Sales_orders, return the CustomerID and the CohortMonth: the first day of the month of the customer's first OrderDate.
questions.hint: MIN(OrderDate) per customer gives the first order. DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(x), MONTH(x), 1) turns a date into the first day of its month.

questions.title: Cohort sizes
questions.story: How many new customers does each monthly cohort have? Return the CohortMonth and the number of customers.
questions.hint: Use the query from the last question as a CTE, then COUNT(*) grouped by CohortMonth.

questions.title: Active customers by month since first order
questions.story: For each cohort, count the customers who ordered in each month after their first. Return the CohortMonth, MonthsSinceFirst (0 for the first month) and the number of different active customers.
questions.hint: List the months in which each customer ordered (DISTINCT customer and month), join it to the first order month, and use DATEDIFF(month, cohort month, order month).

questions.title: Cohort table, months 0 to 3
questions.story: Reshape the last result into a cohort table: one row per cohort with four columns, month0, month1, month2 and month3. Each column holds the number of different customers who ordered that many months after their first order.
questions.hint: Conditional aggregation: COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN MonthsSinceFirst = 1 THEN CustomerID END) for each column.

questions.title: Retention rates and what they show
questions.story: Add the retention rate to the cohort table. Return the CohortMonth, the cohort size and the retention rate for months 1, 2 and 3 as a percent of the cohort size, rounded to 1 decimal. The data ends on 2014-06-30, so a month that has not happened yet must show NULL, not 0. Then answer: for each cohort, is there anything special?
questions.hint: Retention rate = active customers in that month / cohort size (month0). Show a rate only when the cohort month plus the number of months is on or before 2014-06-01, otherwise leave the CASE without an ELSE.
